To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
EGF induces FN and its mRNA in rat liver cells, but cyclic AMP or dextramethasone do not, and that the RNA contains the sequences characteristic of cellular FN.
EGF induces FN synthesis in a cell line that expresses the protein at a very low basal level.
EGF, but not dexamethasones or cyclic AMP, induces FN in liver epithelial cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the expression of the extracellular matrix protein, fibronectin, in liver epithelial cells by EGF, cyclic AMP and glucocorticoids.
the induction and modulation of FN expression in rat liver epithelium.
the mechanism by which EGF induces FN expression and deposition, and the role of FN in the process of cell migration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the EGF‐inducible FN in rat liver epithelia is a cellular form, and that the induction is not mediated by cyclic AMP or glucocorticoid.
EGF‐induction of FN is not mediated by dexamethazone or cyclic AMP.
the expression of cellular fibronactin in rat liver epithelia cells is induced only by EGF.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the EGF‐inducible FN is not regulated by cyclic AMP or by dexamethason, and that EGF induces FN in rat liver epithelium by increasing the rate of transcription of the FN gene.
EGF induces FN in liver epithelial cells by a pathway that is independent of the factors that modulate FN expression elsewhere.
in the liver, FN is induced by EGF, a factor that stimulates cell migration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
EGF‐induction of FN is independent of the factors known to regulate FN expression in other cell types.
EGF‐inducible FN is not identical to the EIIIA/EIIIB‐containing FN found in other cells.
the EGF‐induction of FN is independent of the induction of FN mRNA and is therefore not mediated by the transcriptional activation of a specific gene.
